lines.title: This is Lantern Run, a Halloween roguelike built with Kiro for Kiroween.
lines.menu: You are a jack-o'-lantern, carrying a flame through four haunted rooms. The flame is your only life.
lines.dark: Every room is dark. Your lantern lights the way, and the walls cast real shadows.
lines.candy: The flame burns down over time. Candy restores it, and once you have enough, the door opens.
lines.ghosts: Ghosts drain your flame. Press space to blow them back.
lines.upgrade: After each room, you pick one of three upgrades. Some are trade-offs, like Hungry Flame: more flame from candy, but it burns faster.
lines.patch: Each room has its own lights. Carved pumpkins glow in the pumpkin patch.
lines.smart: Chase ghosts find a path around walls, and blink ghosts fade out just before they teleport.
lines.graveyard: In the graveyard, spirit candles burn on the headstones.
lines.boss: The last room belongs to the Pumpkin King. He winds up, then dashes along a red warning line. Step aside.
lines.win: Reach the door with enough candy, and the King retreats.
lines.result: Your score and upgrades wait at the end, and your best score is saved.
lines.lose: But if your flame goes out, the light shrinks to nothing, and the run is over.
lines.touch: It also plays on phones, with a joystick and a blow button.
lines.kiroSpec: Kiro shaped the whole build. The spec holds fifteen requirement groups and forty-one tasks. When the game turned into a roguelike, we rewrote the spec first, then the code.
lines.kiroSteering: Steering files hold the rules. Core logic never imports Phaser, randomness is always seeded, and the style guide sets the palette and the motion limits.
lines.kiroHooks: Hooks run the type check on every save, and the tests after every task.
lines.kiroPbt: Property-based tests check the rules, from the flame's limits to light that never passes through a wall. All seventy-nine tests pass.
lines.upgrades: There are eight upgrades in all, so every run builds a little differently.
lines.access: Reduced motion follows your browser setting, and hits pulse the screen edges instead of flashing the whole screen.
lines.worked: Specs kept the work organized, steering kept it consistent, and hooks caught problems early. Tests can't tell you if a game is fun, though. That still took playtesting.
lines.outro: Lantern Run is free to play in your browser. Thanks for watching, and happy Kiroween!
lines.madeInCode: Every picture and every sound is made in code. There are no image or audio files, only two open fonts.
